definitions.gloss: hanging strap; strap handle on trains and buses
definitions.explanation: the hanging loops or handles on public transportation that standing passengers hold onto for balance

examples.japanese: {吊|つ}り{革|かわ}につかまって{立|た}っていた。
examples.english: I was standing while holding onto the strap.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}が{揺|ゆ}れたので、{吊|つ}り{革|かわ}をしっかり{握|にぎ}った。
examples.english: The train shook, so I gripped the strap tightly.

examples.japanese: {背|せ}が{低|ひく}くて{吊|つ}り{革|かわ}に{手|て}が{届|とど}かない。
examples.english: I'm too short to reach the hanging strap.

notes:
FORMS:
{吊|つ}る (to hang) + {革|かわ} (leather) → hanging leather

Historically, these straps were made of leather, hence the name. Modern ones are often made of plastic or synthetic materials.
- Triangle-shaped ({三角形|さんかくけい}) - traditional style
- Ring-shaped ({輪|わ}っか{型|がた}) - common on newer trains
- Priority seat straps - often a different color

ADVERTISING:
{吊|つ}り{革|かわ}{広告|こうこく} (strap advertising) refers to advertisements placed on or near the straps, a common form of train advertising in Japan.

RELATED WORDS:
- {手|て}すり (handrail)
- {立|た}ち{客|きゃく} (standing passenger)
- {座席|ざせき} (seat)
